about_the_game:
In Development

The game is still in development, you might notice small bugs and issues, missing textures etc.

The story is fully implemented, and the first case can be played through in its entirety.

Take the role of an investigative journalist in Harlem, in the early 1940s.

Someone has been murdered, and the explanations that the police has come up with just don't add up. Furthermore, the person that the police are accusing of the murder is a good friend of yours, so you'll do anything you can to find out the truth.

Take Pictures

Use your camera to collect evidence; take pictures of anything that seems important to the case.

Organize Your Evidence

See the evidence you collected in your journal, where you can organize and look at the pictures.

Gather Clues And Solve The Case

Talk to people to try and find out what they know. But be careful, some might try to lie to you, and hide the truth. Get their testimonies and piece together the real story

Tell The World

Build your case in the article, and publish it to expose the true killer.

content_descriptors.notes: This game contains depictions of crimes as part of the main mechanic of solving them, and finding the murderer, cause of death, motive etc.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • Requires a 64-bit processor and operating system
  • OS: 10
  • Processor: Intel Core i3-8100 (or AMD Ryzen 3 1200)
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 750 Ti (or AMD Radeon R7 265)
  • DirectX: Version 11
  • Storage: 10 GB available space
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • Requires a 64-bit processor and operating system
  • OS: 10
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-8400 (or AMD Ryzen 5 2600)
  • Memory: 16 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 (or AMD RX 590)
  • DirectX: Version 12
  • Storage: 10 GB available space

short_description: You are a journalist during the Harlem riots, solving cases that just don't seem right. Take pictures of evidence, gather information by talking to people, and put it all together in an article to show people the truth.
